messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Streaming p99 latency spike detected for tenant 'sunrise-health' in us-west-2. Metric: streaming_p99=3200ms (baseline ~600ms). Error rate for streaming frames up 5%. Auto-page: oncall-maya.

maya: on it. paging ryan and sam. any immediate customer reports? @cleo can you check CS channel? :eyes:

cleo: cs-rep confirmed 3 customers (Sunrise prod) reported degraded streaming — partial responses / long stalls. They're seeing partial chunks then long pause.

ryan: jumping in. first ask: is this limited to streaming endpoints or also non-streamed requests?

sam: quick check — non-streaming generation p99 is 700ms, mostly fine. issue looks concentrated on streaming path / websocket multiplex.

alex: I see an uptick in stage 'stream-encoder' queue length on hosts in pool rw-usw2-stream-01..04. KV cache hit ratio stable. CPU on stream workers ~85%, GPU utilization steady. logs show repeated "frame-send-timeout" in stream-agent.

maya: ok so streaming infra. mitigation options: 1) failover tenant to non-streaming (short term) 2) route to fallback model variant that prefers synchronous churn 3) scale additional stream workers 4) enable degraded streaming mode (chunk-size=64). Thoughts?

ryan: agree. immediate priority is reduce customer-visible stalls. Suggest 1) enable non-streaming fallback for sunrise-health via routing policy, 2) spin up +2 stream workers in us-west-2 ASG, 3) collect full stream-agent logs for the window. I'll take 1 and 3. Sam can handle scaling.

sam: scaling ASG now: aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name rw-usw2-stream-workers --desired-capacity 6. putting scale request. ETA ~90s for new workers to be ready.

maya: ryan, can you toggle routing? how to do that quickly?

ryan: doing a policy patch now: 
```bash
# patch routing rule for tenant sunrise-health to fallback non-streaming route
redwoodctl routes update --tenant sunrise-health --route "fallback:non-streaming,model:redwood-3b-v2"
```
Applying...

ryan: patched. sending test request (curl) to validate: 
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"tenant":"sunrise-health","input":"short test","stream":false}' | jq .
```
Got 200 and response latency 420ms.

cleo: CS updated customer: temporary fallback to non-streaming is in place, they see responses but missing streaming UX. Customer accepts for now, asks for ETA on full fix.

alex: collecting stream-agent logs from rw-usw2-stream-0[1-4], grabbing recent 30m window. Suspicious log patterns: repeated backpressure "EPIPE writes" followed by timeouts. Also seeing an increase in websocket frame retransmits from the ingress LB (nginx-ws).

ryan: hypothesis: ingress LB connection churn + stream worker queue growth -> frame stalls. Possible contributing factor: a recent nginx-ws config change rolled 3h ago reduced keepalive timeout to 20s. @sam did we deploy anything in LB config recently?

sam: yes, we rolled nginx-ws update at 11:12 UTC (3h ago) to address memory leak. keepalive changed from 75s -> 20s. rolling back to previous keepalive now.

sam: rollback applied to canary and then to full pool. monitoring LB connection metrics.

maya: good. monitor streaming p99 in next 10m. Also set paging to oncall-esc if p99 > 2s after 10m.

(3m later)

incident-bot: metric update: streaming_p99 now 1.1s (from 3.2s). error rate down to 1.2%.

cleo: Customer reports much improved behavior, streaming working more consistently. They still see occasional small pauses but rate of stalls reduced.

ryan: leaving temporary routing in place until we validate at 24h. plan: 1) keep non-stream fallback for sunrise-health for next 2 hours, 2) fully revert any nginx-ws tuning that reduced keepalive to 75s, 3) add alert for LB connection churn and websocket frame errors, 4) run postmortem if recurrence.

maya: I'll own the post-incident ticket. Action items:
- sam: confirm LB rollback completed and push follow-up fix to avoid memory leak without reducing keepalive (ETA 6h)
- alex: upload stream-agent logs + analysis to incident doc and attach tracers (ETA 2h)
- ryan: keep fallback routing live and draft rollback plan to re-enable streaming when stable (ETA 4h)
- cleo: customer comms summary and SLA impact calc (ETA 1h)

cleo: SLA calc: Sunrise is on Reserved Pro plan. Impact: ~1.5 hours degraded streaming experience for ~30% of requests => estimate 0.03 SLA credit. Drafting note for CS with timeline.

maya: thanks team. Leaving channel open for updates. If metric creeps >2s p99, escalate to oncall-esc.

(incident status: mitigated, monitoring)
